The interior of the hexagon sweeps out an area equal to the original hexagon’s area plus the sum of the sector areas traced by each vertex.  

- Area of a regular hexagon with side 2: \(A_{\text{hex}} = \frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\,s^{2}=6\sqrt3\).  
- Distances from the rotation centre \(O\) to the six vertices give squared distances \(12,28,48,52,36,16\); their sum is \(192\).  
- Each vertex sweeps a sector of angle \(45^\circ = \pi/4\) rad, contributing \(\frac{\theta}{2}r^{2}\) to the area. Hence the total contribution of all vertices is \(\frac{\pi/4}{2}\times192 = 24\pi\).

Adding these parts,
\[
\text{Swept area}=6\sqrt3+24\pi.
\]

ANSWER: \(6\sqrt3+24\pi\)
